To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified two PPR genes that encode ta-siRNAS, and that we experimentally verified the production of these ta-siRNas from the identified PRR genes.
the biogenesis of TAS2 and PPR ta-siRNAta-siRNAs depends on the cleavage of an upstream TAS2 ta-siRNA, which we refer to as a tandem ta-siRNA cascade.
we have (i) developed an algorithm to identify putative TAS genes, (ii) identified two novel TAS genes and (iii) validated their ta-siRNA production and trans-acting activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of a new class of ta-siRNAS and their biogenesis in Arabidopsis.
the discovery of new TAS genes, and it provides a new example of small RNA cascades in plants.
the identification of new small RNA regulatory pathways in plants and the development of a novel computational method for the discovery of novel small RNA genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
miR173 is the master regulator of the TAS genes, which produce ta-siRNA, which in turn regulate the expression of the PPR genes.
the miR173-directed TAS2 cleavage leads to the biogenesis of two ta-siRNA species, which in turn regulate PPR gene expression.
ta-siRNA-directed regulation is not restricted to TAS1, TAS2 and TAS3 genes, but that a TAS2-derived small RNA can direct the production of ta-sRNAs from PPR genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified the first example of a microRNA-initiated small RNA cascade in plants.
we identified a new class of small RNA genes, the PPR genes, and that we found evidence for a small RNA regulatory network that involves the production of ta-sisRNA from the cleavage of ta-siRNAS.
a microRNA can target a TAS gene to generate a ta-siRNA that, in turn, targets another TAS gene, and so on.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the computational prediction of ta-si-siRNAs is possible and that this prediction can be experimentally verified.
the biogenesis of a ta-siRNA from a TAS gene is dependent on the production of a ta-sisRNA from a previously known TAS gene.
the algorithm that we have developed for finding TAS genes can be applied to any species and any small RNA database.
